description: #61: Robin added a Retry budget task whose File ownership row is missing and asks whether it is ready for a worker. The coordinator validates the row with `chief-of-stuff worker --check --root . --task 'Retry budget'`, a read-only call that needs no tree, needs no `--cwd`, creates no worktree and starts nothing, and tells Robin the refusal: the File ownership row is missing. The six graders quote the one sentence that sends a new row to `worker --check` (RED until agents/chief-of-stuff.md carries it, near where `worker` is documented): Before proposing a new task for dispatch, validate its Tasks and File ownership rows with `chief-of-stuff worker --check --root . --task <name>`, which needs no `--cwd`, makes no worktree and starts nothing; add `--name <session>` when the task is a standing row and `--one-shot` for a one-shot task; when it prints `refused: <why>`, tell the user that refusal and do not propose the task. The check grader counts `worker --check` only at the start of a command, in the bare, plugin (`python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/chief_of_stuff.py`) or script-path form, with `--root` and the whole task named; text after `echo`, in a comment or in a quote is not a run. The reply grader accepts, on whole words, any wording that says the File ownership row is missing or absent. A last grader asserts the "do not propose the task" half: a reply that also offers the dispatch (a fenced dispatch prompt, or asking to launch) fails. `--name <session>` (a standing row) and `--one-shot` change what `--check` accepts and are pinned by evals/test_spawn_session.py (CheckTest), not here. What `--check` prints is pinned by evals/test_spawn_session.py (CheckTest), not by this case.
prompt: I just added the Retry budget task to today's tracker. Is it ready to hand to a worker?
